title: Tenant usage simulation and variance attribution audit
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a reproducible simulation harness plus audit jobs to exercise the console backend usage pipelines (token accounting, metering, attribution) across realistic failure modes. The goal is to (1) surface sources of variance between raw usage events and billed tokens, (2) quantify incidence of late-arrival and duplicate tokens, (3) validate attribution heuristics across multi-route and multi-model requests, and (4) produce deterministic testcases and dashboards for regression testing before major runtime or routing changes.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic simulator can inject event streams (on-time, late-arrival, duplicate, partial) against a local copy of the meter/attribution logic
A set of synthetic tenant workloads (chat-heavy, bursty-API, long-context generation, multi-model-split) exists and can be parameterized
A nightly audit job runs on a small set of historical tenant data and reports variance metrics (raw tokens vs billed tokens, attribution mismatch %, late-token rate) to a dashboard
At least three real root-cause categories for variance are identified with reproducible testcases and linked PRs or follow-up tickets
design_notes: Simulator will operate in two modes: replay (from harvested event logs) and stochastic generator (parameterized distributions for arrival skew, duplication, partial payloads)
Keep simulator side-effect free: all test runs use a sandboxed ledger and do not touch production ledgers; data snapshots exported from prod will be scrubbed/hashed
Leverage existing ingestion path but with a 'test' toggle that short-circuits external billing exports and writes to a temp namespace

Trade-offs: deterministic replay is easier to debug but may miss emergent behaviors from timing jitter; stochastic runs help estimate probabilities but require many iterations for statistical confidence
